description:
RA/Dec-to-horizontal (altitude/azimuth) coordinates are computed using the observer's geodetic latitude directly in the spherical-Earth altitude formula, and the satellite look-angle pipeline places the observer at a spherical-Earth ECI position using the equatorial radius and geodetic latitude. This causes systematic errors of ~11 arc-minutes at mid-latitudes — the zenith of a body on the meridian does not match the observer's geodetic latitude because the altitude formula's hour-angle system is geocentric (Earth-centered), not geodetic-vertical-centered.

Expected: When an observer at geodetic latitude φ calculates the altitude of a body whose declination equals the observer's GEOCENTRIC latitude (the latitude of the observer's position vector from Earth's center), and the body is on the local meridian (H=0), the computed altitude should be 90°. The satellite observer ECI position should correctly reflect the WGS84 ellipsoid (geodetic→geocentric lat conversion + height-dependent geocentric radius).

Acceptance criteria:
- equatorialToHorizontal and observerEci accept geodetic lat/lon and internally convert to geocentric latitude before computation, using the WGS84 ellipsoid (a=6378.137 km, f=1/298.257223563) parameters that the codebase already stores as RE/6378.137. [reporter: the issue: observer look-angles use the wrong geodetic model, so WGS84 RA/Dec/alt-az come out wrong]
- The parallax correction in equatorialToHorizontal should use the observer's true geocentric radius (not the fixed equatorial EARTH_RADIUS_AU), computed from the WGS84 ellipsoid. [reporter: the issue: WGS84 RA/Dec/alt-az come out wrong — the parallax uses a spherical Earth radius]
- observerEci must compute the observer's ECI position using the WGS84 ellipsoid (geocentric lat, geocentric radius) instead of the current spherical Earth approximation with geodetic lat and equatorial radius. [code-invariant: src/lib/satellite/look-angles.ts line 10: 'const RE = 6378.137; // km (spherical Earth; ellipsoid/altitude refinement later)' — the code's own comment acknowledges this is a future refinement that is now due]
- The existing Meeus ex. 13.b (Venus, 1987-04-10 19:21 UT, Lat=38.92139°, Lon=-77.06556°) test in src/lib/astronomy/astronomy.test.ts must still pass within the existing tolerance (~0.5°). [baseline: src/lib/astronomy/astronomy.test.ts 'Venus matches Meeus ex. 13.b' — current precision target of ~0.5° with nutation/aberration omitted. The geodetic→geocentric shift (~0.13° at 38.9°N) is within tolerance.]
- A new test must be added: observer at geodetic lat=45°N, lon=0°, with a body at geocentric declination = geocentric latitude of 45°N (~44.81°) on the meridian (H=0), should yield alt ≈ 90°. The exact value must be derived from the WGS84 conversion and stated in the test as the expected value, not invented. [reporter: the issue's first follow-up: 'a body whose declination equals the observer's GEOCENTRIC latitude computes to alt ≈ 90° at H=0']

Domain facts:
- WGS84 ellipsoid: a = 6378137.0 m (equatorial), f = 1/298.257223563 (flattening), b = a×(1−f) ≈ 6356752.314 m (polar). These are international standard values and are not derivable from any file in the repo.
- Geocentric latitude φ' relates to geodetic latitude φ by tan(φ') = (b²/a²)·tan(φ) = (1−f)²·tan(φ)
- Geocentric radius at geodetic latitude φ is R_φ = √[ (a²·cos(φ))² + (b²·sin(φ))² ] / √[ (a·cos(φ))² + (b·sin(φ))² ] — the distance from Earth's center to the observer on the ellipsoid surface (ignoring altitude above the ellipsoid, which the code currently also ignores). At φ=45°, R_φ ≈ 6366 km vs equatorial 6378 km.
- The code currently stores 6378.137 km as the Earth radius in multiple locations (RE = 6378.137 in look-angles.ts and propagate.ts; EARTH_RADIUS_AU = 6378.137/149597870.7 in horizontal.ts). This is the WGS84 equatorial semi-major axis, confirming WGS84 was always the intended model.
